title: Neuroproteasomes regulate endogenous tau paired helical filament formation in an APOE genotype- and age-dependent manner

key_results: Selective neuroproteasome inhibition rapidly triggers de novo formation of endogenous, sarkosyl-insoluble tau PHFs in primary neurons and mouse brain; neuroproteasome abundance is differentially modulated by ApoE isoforms (E2 > E3 > E4) and declines with age; ApoE4 neurons accumulate tau aggregates following modest neuroproteasome disruption while ApoE2 neurons remain resistant
comments: This study elegantly links neuron-specific proteostasis machinery to genetic and age-dependent AD risk factors, positioning neuroproteasome function as a mechanistic convergence point; the therapeutic window for neuroproteasome modulation requires careful investigation.

model_io.model: Primary neurons and mouse brain with APOE genotype variants

hypotheses.hypothesis: Neuroproteasome inhibition impairs tau proteostasis and triggers PHF formation in an APOE genotype-dependent manner
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ApoE4 neurons show greater tau aggregation susceptibility than ApoE2 neurons

hypotheses.hypothesis: Age-related decline in neuroproteasome abundance increases AD risk, particularly in ApoE4 carriers
hypotheses.result: Supported; neuroproteasome levels decrease with age across genotypes

comments: The mechanistic model linking SDC4–Dvl interaction to mitochondrial dysfunction through Wnt pathway inhibition is comprehensive and supported by molecular docking, though the causal pathway from microglial mitochondria to BBB integrity could be further dissected.

hypotheses.result: Supported; BBB integrity correlates with mitochondrial restoration and tight junction protein expression

title: HMGB1 drives pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cell proliferation and migration via the MAP2K3/p38 pathway in pulmonary vascular remodeling
